newsitem.title: USA: PaineWebber cuts '97 natgas forecast to $2.15/MMBtu. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PaineWebber cuts '97 natgas forecast to $2.15/MMBtu. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline from "$2.15 mbtu" to "$2.15 MMBtu" to make clear ammount is expressed in millions of British Thermal Units.)
PaineWebber analyst Rone Barone has cut his price forecast for natural gas for 1997 to $2.15 per million British Thermal Units (BTUs) from $2.30 but is maintaining his 1998 forecast of $2.15.
"We cut our 1997 price forecast because it has been eight percent warmer than average and at these temperatures, people do not need to heat their houses as much," Barone said.
"However, this does not change the long-term fundamentals and I am keeping my 1998 forecast," he added.
Barone has also reduced his cash flow per share estimates for natgas producers.

"We are ahead of Wall Street on this, so there could be some short term weakness in the stocks. Despite the start of a rebound in the group's stock prices yesterday, current market valuations continue to over-compensate for the corresponding reductions in our gas price and earnings and cash flow estimates," he said.
Among pipeline companies, Barone has cut Consolidated Natural Gas Co 1997 estimated cash flow per share to $6.65 from $7.35 and rates the stock a buy.

He has cut Questar Corp cash flow estimates to $5.50 per share from $5.65 and rates it a buy, Sonat Inc cash flow per share has been cut to $7.05 from $7.15 and is rated attractive and Coastal Corp has been cut to $8.55 from $8.60, and is rated attractive.

Among producers, Cabot Oil & Gas Corp cash flow per share has been cut to $2.95 from $3.05 and PaineWebber is neutral on the stock, Enron Oil & Gas Co estimates are $2.60 from $2.95, also neutral, Louisiana Land & Exploration cash flow has been cut to $10.10 from $10.50, and is rated attractive.

Seagull Energy Corp has been cut to $3.95 per share cash flow from $4.20 and PaineWebber is neutral, while Southwestern Energy Co is cut to $3.25 cash flow per share from $3.35 and is rated neutral. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom +1 212 859 1902))
